title: Cedar Bench and Planter Set
description: Add two freestanding cedar planter boxes and a simple cedar bench with cream seat cushions. Keep the existing concrete patio and brick house unchanged. Warm minimalist outdoor lounge, portable planters and no structural additions.

steps.title: Lumber Selection, Milling, and Cut List Preparation
steps.text: Cross-cut all primary lumber components to exact project lengths across the 2x4, 1x4, and 2x2 Western Red Cedar stock according to the cut list before beginning any joinery. Cedar fibers splinter easily, so use sharp saw blades and verify square cuts using a speed square.
actions: Inspect all cedar boards, designating clear and straight faces for exterior slat cladding and structurally sound material for the framing.
Measure and cross-cut eight 18-inch corner posts from the 2x2 Western Red Cedar Lumber using a miter saw or circular saw.
Cross-cut forty 20-inch horizontal wall slats and ten 18.5-inch base floor slats from the 1x4 Western Red Cedar Lumber.
Cut the 2x4 Western Red Cedar Lumber into primary bench frame rails and legs according to final layout dimensions.
Sand cut ends lightly with a random orbital sander with 120-grit sanding discs to eliminate rough saw kerfs and tear-out.
tools: Random orbital sander with 120-grit sanding discs
checks: Verify each cut board end is clean, splinter-free, and exactly 90 degrees relative to board edges using the speed square.
Group matching parts together and verify matching lengths to within 1/16 inch.
stopConditions: Stop cutting if board cupping or warping causes cuts to bind or deviate significantly from square.
Pause if boards split during cutting; adjust blade depth or replace dull blade before continuing.

steps.title: Planter Box Corner Frame and Base Slat Assembly
steps.text: Construct internal upright corner assemblies and bottom support structures for both planter boxes. Pre-drilling is essential in cedar to prevent cracking near board ends.
actions: Lay out four 18-inch 2x2 corner posts per planter box on a flat work surface.
Cut internal horizontal bottom ledge cleats from 2x2 Western Red Cedar Lumber to support the planter floor slats.
Pre-drill all attachment points in the 2x2 cleats using a countersink drill bit (pre-drilling cedar) to prevent splits.
Fasten the internal ledge cleats flush along the lower inside edge of the corner posts using Exterior Stainless Steel Wood Screws 2-1/2 in driven with a cordless drill and driver set.
Lay the 1x4 cedar floor slats across the bottom cleats, spacing them roughly 1/2 inch apart for drainage, and secure them with Exterior Stainless Steel Trim Screws 1-5/8 in.
materials: Exterior Stainless Steel Wood Screws 2-1/2 in
Exterior Stainless Steel Trim Screws 1-5/8 in
checks: Check corner post spacing diagonally from corner to corner to confirm the base frame is square.
Confirm internal floor slats have uniform gaps allowing proper water drainage.
stopConditions: Stop if 2x2 cleats begin cracking during screw installation; enlarge pilot holes slightly before proceeding.

steps.title: Attaching Horizontal Cedar Slats to Planters
steps.text: Clad the exterior perimeter of both planters with horizontal 1x4 cedar slats, creating a clean, modern aesthetic that mirrors the horizontal privacy fence.
actions: Begin at the bottom perimeter of the first planter, aligning the bottom 1x4 slat flush with the bottom of the corner framing.
Pre-drill pilot holes 1 inch from board ends using a countersink drill bit (pre-drilling cedar).
Secure the horizontal 1x4 slats into the 2x2 corner posts using Exterior Stainless Steel Trim Screws 1-5/8 in, driving screw heads slightly below flush.
Work upward around all four sides, clamping each row securely with bar clamps (minimum 24 in) to keep lines parallel.
Repeat the identical wrapping process on the second planter box so both units match in height, slat spacing, and corner alignment.
materials: Exterior Stainless Steel Trim Screws 1-5/8 in
checks: Verify all four corner joints on each row overlap or butt tightly with equal margins.
Confirm the total outer box dimensions remain square at 20 inches wide by 20 inches deep.
stopConditions: Stop and realign if slats drift out of level as rows climb up the planter walls.

steps.title: Lining Planters and Installing Drainage Bases
steps.text: Prepare the planter box interiors by securing bottom support slats and fitting permeable landscape fabric to hold soil while enabling continuous water drainage.
actions: Measure and cut interior drainage slats from 1x4 Western Red Cedar Lumber to span the bottom base cleats of both planter boxes.
Secure the drainage floor slats across the bottom cleats leaving 1/2-inch gaps using Exterior Stainless Steel Trim Screws 1-5/8 in driven with the cordless drill and driver set.
Unroll the Porous Landscape Fabric & Internal Liners and cut two oversized pieces to generously cover the base and interior vertical walls of each box.
Fit the fabric snugly into each box interior, folding neat corners to eliminate bulky bunched material.
Secure the fabric perimeter 1 inch below the top slat rim using the heavy-duty staple gun spaced every 3 inches.
materials: Exterior Stainless Steel Trim Screws 1-5/8 in
checks: Verify that bottom floor slats have consistent 1/2-inch drainage gaps to prevent water stagnation.
Ensure landscape fabric is taut against interior surfaces without tearing or gaping at corners.
stopConditions: Stop if landscape fabric tears during stapling; patch or replace the section before introducing soil.

steps.title: Cutting and Pre-Drilling Bench Frame Members
steps.text: Dimension the primary structural members for the outdoor lounge bench and pre-drill all fastening locations to eliminate cedar wood split risk.
actions: Measure and mark four 18-inch bench legs and two 57-inch longitudinal perimeter rails onto 2x4 Western Red Cedar Lumber using the tape measure and speed square.
Cut the bench perimeter rails, cross spreaders, and leg blanks using the miter saw or circular saw, ensuring clean 90-degree square cuts.
Measure and cut internal ledger support cleats from 2x2 Western Red Cedar Lumber to support the eventual bench seat deck.
Mark pilot hole locations on mating ends, spacing each fastener 3/4 inch from board edges.
Pre-drill all attachment holes through the 2x4 and 2x2 members using the cordless drill and driver set fitted with a countersink drill bit (pre-drilling cedar).
checks: Confirm all paired structural frame pieces match in length within 1/16 inch to keep the assembled frame true.
Verify countersink depth allows screw heads to seat slightly below flush without over-boring fragile cedar.
stopConditions: Stop if any board exhibits structural cracking or excessive warp during crosscutting; re-cut using clear material.

steps.title: Assembling Main Bench Legs and Structural Apron
steps.text: Fasten the structural perimeter apron to the four corner legs and brace the central span, creating a rigid base frame that resists racking.
actions: Set two 18-inch 2x4 legs upright on a flat level floor surface and clamp an end rail flush between them using bar clamps (minimum 24 in).
Fasten the end rail to each leg using Exterior Stainless Steel Wood Screws 2-1/2 in driven through the pre-drilled countersinks with the cordless drill and driver set.
Repeat the assembly sequence for the opposing leg pair to create two identical, rigid end frame subassemblies.
Position the two 57-inch longitudinal 2x4 rails between the leg assemblies, clamp securely with bar clamps (minimum 24 in), and check frame diagonals with the tape measure to confirm square.
Drive Exterior Stainless Steel Wood Screws 2-1/2 in through the front and rear apron rails into the vertical corner legs and middle structural cross-tie.
materials: Exterior Stainless Steel Wood Screws 2-1/2 in
checks: Confirm diagonal measurements across the assembled perimeter rectangular frame match exactly.
Verify all four bench legs rest completely flush on the flat surface without rocking.
stopConditions: Stop and adjust clamping immediately if diagonal measurements differ by more than 1/8 inch before fully setting screws.

steps.title: Installing Bench Deck Support Slats and Back Framing
steps.text: Fasten internal ledger rails and seat slats to complete the bench seating platform, then assemble and secure the low-profile cedar backrest framing.
actions: Cut interior support ledgers from 2x2 Western Red Cedar Lumber and secure them flush along the inside lower perimeter of the 2x4 bench apron using Exterior Stainless Steel Wood Screws 2-1/2 in.
Measure, cut, and space five top seat planks from 1x4 Western Red Cedar Lumber evenly across the bench frame opening, leaving uniform 1/4-inch drainage gaps between boards.
Pre-drill pilot holes with a countersink drill bit and secure each seat plank into the support ledgers using Exterior Stainless Steel Trim Screws 1-5/8 in.
Build the vertical back support uprights and top rail using 2x4 Western Red Cedar Lumber, clamping members square before driving Exterior Stainless Steel Wood Screws 2-1/2 in through the rear legs.
materials: Exterior Stainless Steel Wood Screws 2-1/2 in
Exterior Stainless Steel Trim Screws 1-5/8 in
checks: Confirm seat slats have uniform 1/4-inch expansion spacing and all screw heads are driven flush without splitting the cedar.
Check that the backrest frame is square and rigidly tied to the rear legs with no joint racking.
stopConditions: Halt fastening if cedar splits near board ends; pre-drill a wider clearance hole or adjust screw placement inward by 1/2 inch.

steps.title: Sanding and Finishing All Cedar Surfaces
steps.text: Sand all exposed faces, eased edges, and planter surfaces to eliminate roughness, then apply exterior penetrating sealer to protect the cedar from sun and rain exposure.
actions: Sand all flat boards, end grain, and assembled edges on the bench and planter boxes using a random orbital sander with 120-grit sanding discs.
Wipe away all fine cedar sawdust and debris using a clean, dry cloth or soft shop brush.
Stir Outdoor Penetrating Cedar Sealer thoroughly and apply an even, liberal coat across all exterior wood faces using a stain brush or applicator pad.
Allow the initial coat to soak into the wood pores for 20 to 30 minutes, wipe off any excess puddling, and let dry completely according to manufacturer instructions before applying a second coat.
tools: Random orbital sander with 120-grit sanding discs
checks: Inspect wood surfaces by hand to confirm zero splinters, smooth edges, and no visible runs or wet puddles of excess sealer.
stopConditions: Do not apply penetrating sealer outdoors if rain is forecasted within 24 hours or if ambient temperatures fall below 50 degrees Fahrenheit.

steps.title: Final Patio Placement, Soil Filling, and Cushion Fitting
steps.text: Position the bench and flanking planter boxes against the brick wall on the concrete patio, fit the interior fabric liners, fill with soil mix, and arrange the outdoor cushions.
actions: Position the completed bench centered under the patio double window, maintaining at least a 1-inch clearance gap from the brick masonry wall for ventilation.
Place the two cedar planter boxes flanking either side of the bench, checking that the entry doorway and walking path retain at least 36 inches of clear egress.
Line the interior walls and base slats of both planter boxes with Porous Landscape Fabric & Internal Liners, fastening the top edges with a heavy-duty staple gun.
Empty Lightweight Outdoor Potting Mix into both lined planters, filling to within 2 inches of the top rim to prepare for planting.
Place the Outdoor Bench Cushion Set firmly onto the bench seat deck and against the backrest frame, securing any integrated tie-down straps.
checks: Verify the bench and planters sit completely stable without rocking on the concrete patio surface.
Confirm a minimum 36-inch clear walking path is preserved between the planter box and the exterior doorway.
stopConditions: Do not fill planters directly with garden topsoil if lightweight potting mix is unavailable, as heavy field soil impedes container drainage and overloads wooden slats.

assumptions: The concrete patio is level, crack-free, and drains water away from the foundation naturally.
The bench and planters are entirely freestanding with no mechanical anchoring into the brick veneer or concrete slab.
Potting mix and decorative plants are added after building and placing the units.
All lumber used is naturally rot-resistant Western Red Cedar or equivalent outdoor-rated softwood.
Time is a planning allowance: 10–16 total person-hours; 1 people working 6 productive hours each/day is roughly 2–3 workdays. Waiting for curing, inspections, weather and deliveries is additional.

Reference USD prices, not supplier quotes. Whole stock/boxes/rolls are rounded up before pricing; bulk increments and minimum orders need supplier confirmation. Range is 80–140% of priced purchase quantities, not a guaranteed quote; excludes labor, tax, delivery, rentals and permits.
warnings: Pre-drill all screw holes in cedar; cedar splits very easily near board edges and ends if driven without pilot holes.
Ensure planters have adequate drainage holes lined with fabric to prevent standing water from rotting the floor slats and staining the concrete patio.
Maintain at least a 1-inch air gap between the furniture and the exterior brick wall to avoid trapping exterior wall moisture or debris.
